entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nicholas of Lorraine, Duke of Lorraine (nicholas-i-duke-of-lorraine), was a 15th-century French nobleman and military leader who played a significant role in the Wars of the Burgundian Succession. 

He was born in the 1450s to John II, Duke of Lorraine, and Marie de Bourbon, and succeeded his father as Duke of Lorraine in 1465. 

Nicholas's military campaigns in the Burgundian territories, particularly in the region of Picardy, were marked by his strategic alliances and tactical victories. His most notable achievement was the defeat of the French army at the Battle of Neufchâteau in 1465, which secured his claim to the Duchy of Lorraine. 

As a prominent member of the Burgundian Circle, Nicholas collaborated with other powerful nobles, including Philip the Good, Duke of Burgundy, and Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, to maintain the balance of power in the region. 

His legacy extended beyond his military conquests, as he also promoted the arts and culture, supporting the work of prominent artists and architects of the time. 

Despite his significant contributions, Nicholas's life was cut short when he died in 1473, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the course of Lorraine's history for generations to come.
